Subject: Intermittent short responses in prod

Hi Hannah,

We're seeing intermittent very short completions from the Redwood API in our checkout flow over the last 12 hours — responses like 'OK' or single-word answers instead of the expected multi-sentence recommendation. This is happening across a handful of user sessions (see attached screenshot) and one of our request IDs: req_20270330_aa7f.

Sample prompt (sanitized):
POST /v1/completions
{... prompt: "Suggest upsell for cart items: [***]" ...}

Sample (truncated) response: 200 OK
{ "id": "resp_1", "text": "OK" }

Attachments: screenshot_20270330.png (image/png)

Can you confirm whether this looks like a platform problem or something on our side? We're seeing a small but visible increase in abandonment.

Thanks,
Jill Turner
Head of Product Ops
Acme Retail

From: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>

Cc: (internal)
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 11:02:05 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intermittent short responses in prod — triage notes

Triage summary (attempted reproductions during the reported window):
- Reproductions: NOT REPRODUCIBLE on our side.
- Platform logs: Pulled logs for req_20270330_aa7f and the two-minute window around it. No server-side errors, no fallback to a smaller model, no internal truncation recorded. Token counts and model selection matched the expected config for Acme's route.
- Rate limits / throttling: No anomalies; no 429s for the route.
- Queue/backpressure: Normal. Latencies within historical baselines.

Two observations:
1) In one adjacent request from the same origin, we see a client-side Connect timeout at the network layer (client dropped connection before full response arrived). That pattern can look like 'short output' depending on how the SDK handles partial reads.
2) The customer's screenshot shows the UI rendering a single word. Our logs show the full completion tokenized and returned to the client for req_20270330_aa7f (attached excerpt).

Attachments: logs_session_382.txt (redacted server logs excerpt)

Recommended next steps:
- Advise Acme to capture the raw request body and the full response payload (including headers) for any future occurrences.
- Suggest they check SDK version and network timeouts (we have a known case where certain older SDK versions perform aggressive truncation on early connection drops).
- If they can reproduce again, ask for the request_id + timestamp so we can correlate immediately.

Conclusion: evidence points toward a client-side/network artifact rather than a platform-generation bug. I don't see platform cause from our logs.

— Stephanie
Support Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Hannah Schmitt <hannah@redwood.ai>
To: Jill Turner <jill.turner@acme-retail.com>
Cc: stephanie_nguyen <stephanie@redwood.ai>, sean_gallagher <sean@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Apr 2027 16:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Intermittent short responses in prod — final update

Hi Jill — thanks again for reporting this and for the screenshot. Final update from our triage team:

- We reviewed the request_id you provided and ran reproductions during the same time window. Our server-side logs show the full completion was generated and delivered to Acme's client for req_20270330_aa7f. (See attached log excerpt).
- We did not find evidence of model fallback, token truncation, or a runtime generation error on Redwood.
- We did note one adjacent request where the client connection timed out early (Connect timeout) which can cause the client-side SDK to surface an incomplete UI value while the platform still generated the full text.

Recommended actions for Acme:
1) If it happens again, capture and share the raw request and the full response headers/body (or at least the request_id and timestamp).
2) Upgrade to the latest Redwood SDK (we've seen older SDKs incorrectly surface partial data on early disconnects).
3) Consider logging the response length and response headers in the UI layer to help differentiate between server returns vs client truncation.

Given the results, we consider this incident closed on the platform side. If you disagree or you collect a new example that looks different from the pattern above, please re-open the ticket and send the extra artifacts.

Thanks — and sorry for the disruption.

Best,
Hannah Schmitt
Senior Customer Success Manager
Redwood Inference
